## What this analysis does

This site explains the R analysis of the EM-ASTHMA pilot randomized trial, which compared the COHERO mobile app with control. Participants included adults and children with a caregiver. Assessments were scheduled at baseline and 2, 4, 6, 9 and 12 months. The analysis asks how outcomes differ between the assigned groups and whether those differences vary over time or between subgroups.

There are two main kinds of outcome. Questionnaire scores describe asthma control, quality of life, activity limitation and self-reported controller adherence at repeated visits. App medication records and health-care-use fields supply counts and measures of recorded use. Those different data structures need different statistical models.

The detailed intervention, eligibility criteria and choice of a primary outcome still need protocol information; the code alone cannot establish them. This site explains the implemented analysis and does not report trial findings.

## How to read this site

If you have some R and introductory statistics experience, start with [Longitudinal data and mixed models](quarto/methods_longitudinal.qmd). Then read [Interactions](quarto/methods_interactions.qmd) and [What a p-value for interaction means](quarto/methods_interaction_p_values.qmd). You can skip the optional algebra in [Effects behind an interaction](quarto/methods_stratified_effects.qmd) on a first pass.

The **Code** pages follow the order of `R/main.R`. Each explains the input, the operation and the output before showing code imported from the actual script. Code is folded so you can read the explanation first. Opening a code block does not run it. The Methods examples use illustrative object names and invented numbers; they are not copy-and-run analyses of this trial.

[Braces](https://forum.posit.co/t/curly-braces-around-package-name-convention/122547) identify R packages throughout this site.

## Follow the rows

| Stage | What a row represents | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Imported visit data | A participant at a recorded visit | Several rows can belong to the same person |
| App medication records | A recorded medication event | Many records must be summarized before comparing participants |
| Participant-day grid | A candidate day for a participant | Days without records affect the adherence denominator |
| Count-model data | A participant with counts and follow-up time | Time at risk matters when comparing counts |
| Mixed-model data | A participant at a visit | The model accounts for repeated measurements within a person |

The grid and several other derivations still have issues under review. The pages describe the present code rather than assuming those issues are fixed.

## Terms used throughout

| Term | Meaning here |
|---|---|
| Arm | The assigned intervention or control group |
| Baseline | The starting assessment |
| Intention to treat (ITT) | Comparing participants by assigned arm, using available observations |
| Per protocol (PP) | This project's restriction to observations on or before the app-glitch cutoff; not a general definition of adherence |
| Subgroup | A participant characteristic used to ask whether the arm effect differs between groups |
| ACT / AQLQ / PACQLQ / AFS | Code labels for asthma control, adult quality of life, caregiver quality of life, and activity limitation; exact instrument versions and scoring rules still need verification |
| PDC | Proportion of days covered; here calculated from recorded controller use, as explained on the medication page |
| Confidence interval | An interval describing uncertainty in an estimated effect; its meaning depends on the model and assumptions |

For R syntax, [R for Data Science](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/) is a free reference with worked examples [@r4ds2]. You only need the linked topic when it helps with the section you are reading.

## Status

The project is being ported from an earlier R Markdown analysis into plain R scripts. The pipeline has completed a synthetic-data check; that checks execution on invented inputs, not agreement with the original analysis or validity on study data. Known defects and decisions are tracked in [Issues](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/COHERO-RCT-analysis/issues).

The [analysis plan](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/COHERO-RCT-analysis/blob/main/analysis-plan.md) records the scientific specification retrospectively. The study files and participant-derived outputs are not provided on this site. Clinical background and study-design pages will follow when the necessary source information is available.
